open_points.subject: owner authentication
open_points.text: Reaches the kernel through the agent channel with the owner's token.
open_points.question: Who provisions, stores, rotates and revokes the owner's token, and how does the kernel distinguish it from an agent token?
options: The installation operator manages a distinct owner token
The owner token is one specially marked configured token
The reverse proxy authenticates the owner and supplies an identity
open_points.default_guess: Use a distinct owner token managed in protected installation configuration and re-read it after configuration changes.

open_points.subject: installation administration
open_points.text: agent token configured in the installation
open_points.question: Which actor is authorized to configure service credentials, owner and agent tokens, manifest instances and the kernel listener?
options: The owner administers the installation
A separate installation operator administers it
The hosting platform administers it from declarative configuration
open_points.default_guess: Treat the owner as the installation administrator.

open_points.subject: platform manifest
open_points.text: Microservices — known only as records of the platform manifest.
open_points.question: Where does the manifest come from, who is trusted to change it, how is its authenticity established, and when does the kernel observe a change?
options: A trusted local installation file re-read on every relevant request
A signed manifest supplied by a platform service
A manifest loaded once at process startup
open_points.default_guess: Use a trusted local installation file and detect changes before proposals, acceptances and invocations.

open_points.subject: authentication failures
open_points.text: Each action names its observable output and its failure.
open_points.question: What observable refusal is returned for a missing, invalid or revoked token, an owner token used for an agent-only action, or an agent lacking the required author right?
options: One authentication or authorization refusal with a reason
Distinct unauthenticated and forbidden refusals
The reverse proxy rejects missing or invalid credentials before the kernel
open_points.default_guess: Return distinct unauthenticated and forbidden refusals without creating domain records.

open_points.subject: author permission scope
open_points.text: Reads, authors functions and flows, requests trials, runs flows. Holds an agent token configured in the installation; the token says whether the agent may author.
open_points.question: Does the may-author flag govern flow composition and binding proposals as well as functions and trial cases, given that those Primary actions allow any agent?
options: It governs every authoring action, including flows and binding proposals
It governs only function contracts, implementations and trial-corpus changes
Flows and binding proposals have separate rights
open_points.default_guess: Apply may-author to functions, trial-corpus changes, flows and binding proposals.

open_points.subject: secret echoed by a service
open_points.text: A service's own answer body that echoes one verbatim is withheld from everyone, the owner included, and never used as an output
open_points.question: When a response body is withheld for containing a credential, what status, failure code, trace information and downstream behavior result?
options: Fail the operation node with a secret-disclosure refusal
Treat the service response as invalid and fail the run
Rest the run pending for owner intervention
open_points.default_guess: Fail the operation node and record only a bounded secret-disclosure reason.

open_points.subject: agent-to-service access
open_points.text: the agent processes a photo itself, outside the kernel, with its own access to the service that holds the photo
open_points.question: What actor grants and controls this direct agent-to-microservice access, and how is it compatible with the statement that the owner is the only reader of personal data?
options: Direct access is outside this product and must independently enforce the same disclosure rule
Only the owner may perform that outside processing when the photo is personal data
The service supplies a separate redacted or delegated agent interface
open_points.default_guess: Treat direct access as an external trust boundary that independently prevents agents from reading personal data.

open_points.subject: contract-version succession
open_points.text: the first contract of a new slot name creates the slot
open_points.question: What makes a later contract version the slot's current contract version, and what happens to the existing implementation activation when that occurs?
options: Authoring a new contract version immediately makes it current and leaves it without an activation
A separate activation or promotion action makes a contract version current
A slot can have only one contract version
open_points.default_guess: Authoring a later contract version makes it current and leaves it inactive until an implementation is admitted.

open_points.subject: content equality
open_points.text: an existing one when the content is equal
open_points.question: Within what scope and by what canonical representation are contracts, implementations and trial cases considered equal?
options: Canonical typed serialization within the named slot or contract version
Raw submitted bytes within the whole installation
Semantic equality after normalization
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical typed serialization scoped to the relevant slot or contract version.

open_points.subject: trial-case oracle
open_points.text: add a trial case
open_points.question: What does a trial case contain besides port-fitting values, including the expected output or expected failure against which an implementation passes?
options: Inputs plus exact expected outputs
Inputs plus output predicates encoded by the contract
Inputs asserting only successful schema-valid execution
open_points.default_guess: Store inputs and exact expected outputs, including file fixtures where applicable.

open_points.subject: captured failure oracle
open_points.text: capture a failed execution into the trial corpus
open_points.question: How can a failed execution become a case that later implementations must pass when the failed execution supplies no correct expected output?
options: Capture only the input and require later schema-valid success
Require the owner or authoring agent to provide expected outputs when capturing
Capture the precise failure as an outcome that must not recur
open_points.default_guess: Capture the input and define passing as completing successfully with contract-valid output.

open_points.subject: eligible captured execution
open_points.text: an execution that succeeded, was skipped, belongs to another contract version, or whose run was already released ... is refused
open_points.question: Is capture restricted to failed function-node executions, or can failures of operation, map or guard nodes also be captured?
options: Only failed function-node executions
Any failed node associated with a function contract
All node failures with a conversion defined per node kind
open_points.default_guess: Restrict capture to failed function-node executions.

open_points.subject: corpus mutation after admission
open_points.text: the trial case every later implementation must pass
open_points.question: When a trial case is added or captured after an implementation was admitted and activated, does the old verdict remain valid, is the activation suspended, or is admission rerun automatically?
options: Existing verdicts and activations remain valid; only later submissions use the enlarged corpus
All verdicts become stale and the active implementation is readmitted automatically
All verdicts become stale and the contract version has no activation until explicit resubmission
open_points.default_guess: Keep the existing activation valid but require any later admission or rollback to use the enlarged corpus.

open_points.subject: operation effect class
open_points.text: Effect classes are `read`, `draft-write`, `state-transition`, `external-effect`, `destructive`.
open_points.question: Where is an operation's effect class declared, who is trusted to choose it, and is it pinned by the accepted binding?
options: The manifest operation record declares it and the binding pins it
The proposing agent declares it and the owner accepts it
The owner assigns it separately after accepting the binding
open_points.default_guess: Declare it in the manifest operation record and include it in the binding's pinned digest.

open_points.subject: operation idempotency
open_points.text: The kernel supplies the declared idempotency key
open_points.question: Where and how does an operation declare support for an idempotency key, how is the key transported, and what happens if an effectful operation lacks that declaration?
options: The manifest declares a header or body field and effectful bindings without it are refused
The kernel always sends one fixed header
Only selected effect classes require service-declared idempotency
open_points.default_guess: Require each effectful manifest operation to declare the key's request location and refuse a binding that does not.

open_points.subject: accepted binding withdrawal
open_points.text: only the owner accepts it
open_points.question: How can the owner disable or revoke an accepted binding that was accepted mistakenly or is no longer trusted?
options: Add an owner revoke-binding action
Accepting a replacement binding supersedes it
Only changing or removing the manifest operation can stop it
open_points.default_guess: Add an owner action that revokes an accepted binding and prevents new invocations.

open_points.subject: manifest drift during a run
open_points.text: When that digest no longer matches, invocation is refused until a new binding is accepted
open_points.question: What observable node and run state results when a pinned binding no longer matches at invocation time: failed, pending, or refused without a run?
options: Fail the node and eventually the run
Rest the run pending until a new binding is accepted and it is resumed
Refuse the run before creating it if any binding is already stale
open_points.default_guess: Refuse the run before creation when detectable at start; otherwise fail the affected node.

open_points.subject: missing service instance
open_points.text: an installation may leave a service without an instance; that service is not invocable, and no binding for it can be proposed or accepted
open_points.question: What happens to an already accepted binding and to a pinned run when the selected service instance is removed?
options: The binding remains accepted but invocation rests pending as unreachable
The binding becomes unusable and invocation fails
Existing runs retain the removed instance while new runs refuse
open_points.default_guess: Keep the binding record accepted and treat invocation as pending because the service is unavailable.

open_points.subject: flow external interface
open_points.text: A flow's own inputs and outputs are values, never files
open_points.question: How are a flow version's input and output ports declared, typed, classified and connected to graph nodes when the listed graph forms contain only edges, maps and guards?
options: Flow versions have explicit typed input and output ports
Special source and sink nodes represent the interface
Inputs and outputs are inferred from unconnected node ports
open_points.default_guess: Give each flow version explicit typed and classified value input and output ports.

open_points.subject: flow-version identity
open_points.text: the flow version and its proof result
open_points.question: Does composing content identical to an existing version return that version, create a new version, or refuse it?
options: Return the existing content-addressed version
Create a new monotonically numbered version
Refuse duplicate content
open_points.default_guess: Return the existing content-addressed version.

open_points.subject: first proof failure
open_points.text: the first failing edge or node
open_points.question: What deterministic ordering defines the first failure in a graph with parallel branches?
options: Canonical node and edge identifier order
Topological order with a defined tie-breaker
Submission order
open_points.default_guess: Use canonical topological order with identifier order as the tie-breaker.

open_points.subject: map semantics
open_points.text: a map of a node over a collection
open_points.question: What are the map's input and output shapes, ordering, concurrency, bounds and failure semantics when one mapped item fails or waits?
options: Ordered collection in and ordered collection out; any item failure fails the map after independent items finish
Fail fast on the first item failure
Represent each mapped item as an independently traced execution with partial results
open_points.default_guess: Preserve order, trace each item, allow independent items to finish, and fail the map if any item fails.

open_points.subject: guard semantics
open_points.text: a guard on a declared closed value
open_points.question: What value is tested, how branches are represented, what happens to the unselected branch, and how is a value outside the closed set handled?
options: Match an enum value to named branches and mark unselected nodes skipped
A guard conditionally enables one node only
An unmatched value is a proof failure rather than a run-time failure
open_points.default_guess: Match a declared enum value to named branches, mark other branches skipped, and fail validation if the runtime value is outside the schema.

open_points.subject: standing-approval eligibility
open_points.text: grant a standing approval for a node of a flow's active version
open_points.question: Which effect classes may receive a standing grant, given that read and draft-write normally do not ask and destructive explicitly cannot be granted?
options: Only `state-transition` and `external-effect`
`draft-write`, `state-transition` and `external-effect`
Every class except `destructive`
open_points.default_guess: Allow grants only for `state-transition` and `external-effect` nodes.

open_points.subject: grant lifetime across activation changes
open_points.text: the node of that flow version stops asking, or asks again
open_points.question: Does a non-revoked grant remain usable by runs pinned to that version after another version becomes active, and does it become usable again if the old version is reactivated?
options: The grant remains attached to the exact version until explicitly revoked
The grant ends automatically when that version ceases to be active
Existing pinned runs retain it, but later reactivation requires a new grant
open_points.default_guess: Keep the grant attached to the exact version until explicitly revoked, including for pinned runs and later reactivation.

open_points.subject: approval decision preconditions
open_points.text: an approval of a run that has ended can no longer be decided
open_points.question: What happens when the referenced attempt is not awaiting approval, was already decided, or its built request changed before the owner decides?
options: Refuse with a reason and leave the current run state unchanged
Return the existing decision idempotently when already decided
Void the stale approval and create a new approval request automatically
open_points.default_guess: Return an existing identical decision idempotently; otherwise refuse stale or inapplicable decisions and leave or restore the run to `awaiting_approval` for the current request.

open_points.subject: cancellation during execution
open_points.text: the run ends `cancelled`; nothing further is sent
open_points.question: What happens if a function or HTTP operation is already executing when cancellation arrives, particularly when an effect request may already have left the kernel?
options: Cancellation prevents only future sends and records the in-flight attempt's eventual outcome
Cancellation waits for the current node to finish before ending the run
Cancellation terminates functions but cannot retract HTTP requests already sent
open_points.default_guess: Terminate sandbox functions where possible, never send later requests, and record any already-sent operation attempt independently of the cancelled run.

open_points.subject: trace lookup
open_points.text: read a trace | owner, agent | trace records | —
open_points.question: What identifies the requested trace or trace set, and what is returned for an unknown or unauthorized reference?
options: Read by run and optional node/attempt identifiers; unknown reference is refused
Read only through general inspection filters
Unknown references return an empty collection
open_points.default_guess: Read by run plus optional node or attempt identifier and return an unknown-reference refusal.

open_points.subject: repair and composition context
open_points.text: For repair an agent receives one contract, its current implementation and that slot's recent traces and trial evidence; for composition, contracts, bindings and not implementation bodies.
open_points.question: Which Primary action requests these two context views, how is the one repair slot selected, what does recent mean, and what are their observable failures?
options: They are defined inspect queries with explicit slot and bounded pagination
The kernel pushes them automatically when repair or composition begins
Separate repair-context and composition-context actions exist
open_points.default_guess: Define them as typed inspect queries with an explicit slot, deterministic bounded pagination and unknown-reference failures.

open_points.subject: fixed MCP surface
open_points.text: The kernel exposes one fixed set of typed operations over `mcp`: inspect, author, try, run, resume, read traces, and the owner's approve, accept, activate, grant, revoke, resolve and cancel.
open_points.question: How are add-trial, capture-failure, release-failed-run, rollback-slot, propose-binding, compose-and-prove, refuse-effect and agent-or-owner release/rollback exposed when they are Primary actions but absent or assigned differently in this supposedly fixed set?
options: Each is a distinct MCP operation and K-11's list must include it
They are explicitly defined variants of broader `author`, `inspect`, `approve` or `activate` operations
Some Primary actions are intentionally unavailable over MCP
open_points.default_guess: Expose every Primary action as a distinct typed MCP operation and make K-11's inventory exhaustive.

open_points.subject: deactivating executable state
open_points.text: active flow version
open_points.question: How can the owner stop new runs of an active flow, or remove a function activation when no safe rollback implementation exists?
options: Add deactivate-flow and deactivate-contract-version actions
Activation can only be replaced, never removed
Revoking agent tokens and cancelling individual runs are the only stop mechanisms
open_points.default_guess: Add owner actions to deactivate a flow version and clear a function activation without deleting their records.

open_points.subject: service response failures
open_points.text: their answers are untrusted data until validated at the port
open_points.question: What observable node and run outcomes distinguish an unreachable service, an HTTP error, malformed response, schema violation, disclosure violation and secret-bearing response?
options: Only transport unreachability is pending; all received invalid responses fail the node
All service failures are pending and resumable
A binding declares which HTTP responses are retryable or terminal
open_points.default_guess: Treat absence of a response as resumable `pending`; treat received HTTP or validation failures as terminal node failures.

open_points.subject: classification of non-service values
open_points.text: Every value carries `open`, `business_confidential` or `personal_data`.
open_points.question: Who assigns and validates the class of flow inputs, constants, guard values, trial values and file fixtures that do not originate in a binding response?
options: Their declaring contract or flow port fixes the class
The caller labels each supplied value
The kernel derives the class from provenance
open_points.default_guess: Fix the accepted class on each declared port and require supplied values to carry a class no lower than their trusted provenance.

open_points.subject: zero-input function classification
open_points.text: a function's output takes the highest class its execution received
open_points.question: What class does a function output receive when the function has no inputs?
options: `open`
A class declared on the output port
Zero-input functions are forbidden
open_points.default_guess: Classify it as `open` unless the contract declares a higher fixed output class.

open_points.subject: Python execution environment
open_points.text: Functions are written in Python only.
open_points.question: Which Python implementation and version are contracts admitted and later run against, and is that runtime identity pinned so deterministic admission and run replay survive upgrades?
options: The installation pins one exact Python runtime version and runs pin it
Each implementation declares a supported Python version
The current kernel runtime is used without version pinning
open_points.default_guess: Pin an exact Python runtime identity in the installation and include it in admission evidence and run provenance.

open_points.subject: standard-library boundary
open_points.text: the Python standard library only
open_points.question: Which standard-library modules are unavailable because they expose forbidden network, filesystem, clock, randomness, process or secret capabilities, and what failure is produced when code imports or reaches one?
options: A fixed allowlist of capability-safe standard-library modules
All standard-library modules are importable but sandbox controls block forbidden effects
A fixed denylist excludes capability-bearing modules
open_points.default_guess: Use a versioned allowlist and report a sandbox violation for imports or calls outside it.
